gotchas: Positive finding, not an absence of research: the complete vendor manual was extracted and searched, and it documents no communications hardware of any kind. The Brat's entire user interface is four LEDs (Bulk, Float, Load On, Low Battery) with patterned blinking for fault codes, plus DIP-style switches. 30 A PWM, 12/2

It does have interesting behaviour worth recording for the no-comms file — a "Solar Clock" that learns sunrise and sunset over a seven-day monitoring cycle and then switches loads at dusk and dawn — but all of it is internal. There is no way to read it.
Recorded here so nobody researches it twice. A driver is not possible without added hardware (a shunt and a separate meter), which makes it a no-comms entry, not a future dialect.
